subject: Bridgeway integration: safe path for SDK/contract changes
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@bridgeway.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@bridgeway.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: SDK breaking change notice & ask: migration window and compatibility guarantees

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from Bridgeway: our engineering team is seeing an upcoming Redwood SDK/contract change in the product roadmap that looks like it will remove v2 behavior and introduce a new streaming contract (what your team called "stream-v3") in Q3. We have an active integration used by multiple joint customers and need to understand a few things to avoid regressions: 

- Can you share the proposed deprecation timeline and what will constitute a breaking change vs a minor semver bump?
- Will Redwood publish compatibility shims or a compatibility-test harness we can run in CI?
- Are there flags or migration guides that let us opt into the new behavior behind a toggle?

We attached an impact matrix (bridgeway-sdk-impact-matrix.xlsx) with the endpoints/features we rely on. Our ask: a mutual action plan and a 60–90 day migration window with canary guidance so we can update our SDK and notify customers.

Would you and the SDK/product folks be available for a 30–45m sync early next week?

Thanks,
Aisha Kapoor
Head of Integrations, Bridgeway Analytics
Aisha.kapoor@bridgeway.ai

[Attachment: bridgeway-sdk-impact-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@bridgeway.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK breaking change notice & ask: migration window and compatibility guarantees

Thanks for the matrix, Aisha — very helpful. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

1) Timeline: we are targeting an opt-in beta for the new streaming contract in mid-July, with full removal of the legacy v2 semantics targeted for the Sept maintenance window (Sept 8–12). That gives an intended public deprecation notice of ~8 weeks before removal.

2) Compatibility: we plan to provide two things: (a) a compatibility shim layer for the most common client patterns (token streaming, chunked responses) and (b) a test harness that runs lightweight smoke tests against a compatibility endpoint. Both will be posted to the partner doc space and a short npm/py package will be published.

3) Flags & opt-in: yes — the beta will be behind a feature flag (enable_stream_v3) for Dedicated/private customers and behind a header toggle for hosted customers so you can opt-in per-tenant.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick sync Wed 2027-05-26 10:00 PT — 30m to review the matrix and nail ownership for each impacted endpoint.
- We’ll circulate a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) after that sync with timeline milestones and responsibilities.
- Camila (runtime) will own the shim work; Vanessa (partnerships) will own the partner comms and SLAs.

Looping in Camila and Vanessa to confirm.

Jonas Weber
Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

On 2027-05-20 Aisha Kapoor wrote:
> Quick note from Bridgeway: our engineering team is seeing an upcoming Redwood SDK/contract change...

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@bridgeway.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK breaking change notice & ask: migration window and compatibility guarantees

Thanks — a few product/partner policy points I want us to bake into the MAP. Draft attached (proposal-compat-policy-draft.docx). High level:

- Breaking-change policy: Major contract changes (where payload shapes or stream framing change) require a 60–90 day deprecation window and a documented compatibility testing path.
- Semver and deprecation: we will adhere to semver for SDKs and call out any server-side contract changes explicitly in release notes.
- Partner SLA: for named partners with integrations in production we can offer a compatibility-stability SLA (30-day rollback window + priority fixes for regressions during migration).
- Canary guidance: seeds for partner canaries (percentage-based traffic switches, health check endpoints, and suggested monitoring signals).

Camila: can you confirm the shim scope (protocol-level only, or will it include client-side helpers)? Camila, Jonas — we should also align on what tests are required for the harness (smoke vs. end-to-end).

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposal-compat-policy-draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@bridgeway.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@bridgeway.ai>, procurement@bridgeway.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK breaking change notice & ask: migration window and compatibility guarantees

Appreciate the concrete items and the draft, Vanessa. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the shim: Bridgeway prefers the shim to be server-side (so our SDKs don't have to maintain per-customer toggles). That reduces lift on our side. Is that feasible?
- Test harness: we can contribute a set of integration tests (attached) that exercise our most common payloads if you provide an endpoint and a lightweight runner.
- Customer comms: we will co-author a migration guide and want it to include sample-code snippets for JS/Python, a migration checklist, and a rollback playbook.

We attached a first pass of test cases (bridgeway-test-cases.json). Can we get the MAP and a proposed timeline by EOD Monday so our PMs can schedule internal work?

Thanks,
Aisha

[Attachment: bridgeway-test-cases.json (JSON)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@bridgeway.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK breaking change notice & ask: migration window and compatibility guarantees

Perfect — thanks Aisha. Quick confirmation of actions and owners, and I’ll drop the MAP link after this message: 

- Shim approach: Camila confirms we will implement the compatibility shim server-side for the top 10 impacted patterns (token streaming, partial-chunk responses, resumable streams). We’ll publish the shim as a service and an opt-in header. (owner: camila_reyes)
- Test harness: we’ll provision a compatibility endpoint and publish a lightweight runner. Please attach your test cases to the runner repo; we’ll run them as part of partner onboarding. (owner: camila_reyes, timeline: beta by 2027-07-15)
- MAP: draft MAP created and posted here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/partner-bridgeway-sync (please review). Final MAP w/ milestones by Monday EOD (2027-05-26).
- Partner comms + SLA: Vanessa will draft the partner communication and the compatibility-stability SLA text; we’ll include it in the MAP. (owner: vanessa_ortiz)
- Follow-up sync: scheduled Wed 2027-05-26 10:00 PT — calendar invite sent.

I’ll include the HubSpot deal link in the MAP (https://hubspot.com/deal/8842) and add the DocuSign stub for the compatibility SLA once Vanessa finalizes wording.

Thanks all — seems like a good plan.

Jonas
